trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use travel time to settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport, take the Aerobus (€5.90) or Metro L9 Sud to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic facades without paying entrance fees.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Eixample grid streets and discover the vibrant local bar scene. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for affordable tapas bars. Ease into Barcelona nightlife at a local cervecería — nights here start late, so a relaxed first evening is ideal.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (sandwich) from a local bakery or supermarket like Mercadona near Eixample (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Bar Calders on Carrer del Parlament — affordable pintxos and tapas, budget around €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) on arrival — it will save money throughout the trip. August is hot in Barcelona (30°C+), so carry water and sunscreen. Nights are warm and lively.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Sagrada Família — book tickets online in advance to save time (€26 basic entry, or €32 with tower access). Arrive when it opens at 9:00 to beat the crowds and the afternoon heat. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's masterpiece, one of the world's most extraordinary architectural achievements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (€10 entry for the Monumental Zone — book online). Explore the mosaic terraces, Hypostyle Room, and panoramic views over Barcelona. After the park, head back toward Gràcia neighborhood and wander its charming squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia — free and full of local life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for dinner, then explore the Eixample 'Gayxample' area around Carrer del Consell de Cent for lively bars. Hit a pre-club bar around 22:00–23:00. For nightlife, check out Antilla BCN Salsa Club or walk along Carrer d'Enric Granados — a pedestrian boulevard with outdoor bars and a buzzing atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Josep bakery near Eixample — coffee and pastry for €4–6
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or Gràcia — 3 courses including drink for €12–14
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — excellent tapas, budget €12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets at least a few days ahead — they sell out fast in August. Wear comfortable shoes; there's significant walking and some uphill terrain at Park Güell.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of the best free architecture experiences in Barcelona. Wander the ancient Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30), Plaça Reial, and narrow medieval lanes. Look for hidden gems like the Temple d'August (free) with Roman columns inside a medieval courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down La Rambla to the waterfront, then explore El Born neighborhood. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning 14th-century Gothic church with free entry. Browse the Mercat de Santa Caterina (colorful mosaic roof, free to view) and duck into the Parc de la Ciutadella for a relaxing break by the lake (free entry). Rent a rowboat on the lake for €6 per person.
day_by_day.evening: El Born is one of Barcelona's best neighborhoods for nightlife. Start with vermouth (vermut) at a local bar around 19:00 — a beloved Barcelona tradition. Then explore the bar-lined streets of El Born after 22:00. Try Bar del Pla or Miralmundo for affordable drinks in a buzzing atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: La Granja on Carrer dels Banys Nous in the Gothic Quarter — famous for hot chocolate and churros, €5–7
meals.lunch: Mercat de la Boqueria on La Rambla — grab fresh fruit, cheese, and cured meats for a budget picnic (€8–10); avoid the tourist stalls and shop from local vendors
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — classic Catalan tapas bar, cava by the glass, budget €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep a close eye on belongings on La Rambla — it is a well-known pickpocket hotspot. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; get lost intentionally for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus to Montjuïc. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 round trip) for stunning panoramic views of the city and port. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) — a historic fortress with incredible architecture and views. Walk the surrounding gardens for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Barceloneta Beach for an afternoon by the sea — free entry. Cool off in the Mediterranean and admire the beachfront architecture including the iconic Hotel Arts tower and Frank Gehry's golden fish sculpture. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade. Optionally, visit the Barceloneta neighborhood's grid of streets — an 18th-century urban planning gem.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta and Port Olímpic come alive at night. Grab drinks at one of the beachfront chiringuitos (beach bars). For a more local nightlife experience, head back to Eixample or El Raval — check out Sala Apolo (one of Barcelona's most iconic music venues) for live music or club nights, entry typically €10–15.

meals.breakfast: Forn de la Trinitat bakery in El Born or a café in Eixample — coffee and toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet) for €4–6
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early — opens at 9:00, often sells out by early afternoon) — birthplace of the bombas, budget €10–13; alternatively grab a bocadillo from a beach kiosk
meals.dinner: La Barceloneta restaurant or any of the affordable seafood spots on Carrer de l'Almirall Aixada — fresh seafood paella or fideuà, budget €13–17 per person

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is best visited in the morning before the heat peaks. Bring a swimsuit and towel for Barceloneta. August crowds at the beach are large — arrive by 16:00 to find good spots. Sala Apolo events vary — check their website in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Casa Vicens in Gràcia (€16 entry) — Gaudí's first major work and a UNESCO-listed gem that receives far fewer visitors than his other buildings. A truly special architectural experience. Afterward, explore the Gràcia neighborhood's charming squares and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Passeig de Gràcia for any last-minute sightseeing or souvenir shopping. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies (€12) for a dose of modern Catalan art housed in a stunning Modernista building, or simply walk the Eixample streets to appreciate the extraordinary density of Modernista architecture — many facades are free to admire from outside. Pack bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Last dinner in Barcelona — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal as a farewell. Head back to a favorite neighborhood or try somewhere new in Eixample. Enjoy a final walk along Passeig de Gràcia at dusk when the Modernista buildings are beautifully lit.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni neighborhood — popular brunch spot, budget €8–12
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in Gràcia — 3 courses with wine for €13–15
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Carrer de de Londres in Eixample — beloved local spot, great value, budget €12–16 per person; or Bodega Sepúlveda for Catalan wine and tapas

day_by_day.notes: If departing the following day, confirm checkout time with the hotel. Keep metro card topped up for airport transfer. Duty-free shopping at Barcelona El Prat Airport is available after security. Save €5–10 for the Aerobus or metro fare back to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on board and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus or metro to your hotel in Eixample. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — featuring Gaudí's Casa Batlló, Domènech i Montaner's Casa Lleó Morera, and Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller — all within walking distance of your hotel. No tickets needed for exterior views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Eixample neighbourhood for your first taste of Barcelona nightlife. Explore the vibrant Gayxample area around Carrer del Consell de Cent for cocktails at a stylish bar, then wind down with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy coffee and a croissant on the plane or grab a quick café con leche and a bocadillo at a café near the airport or metro station upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a mid-range set lunch menu (menú del día) near Eixample — try Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for tapas and montaditos (approx. €15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Parking Pizza or Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample — casual, quality dining with local wines. Budget approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Focus on settling in, orienting yourself around the Eixample grid, and getting a feel for the city. Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport for convenient transport all week.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — both are within walking distance of your hotel in Eixample. Opt for Casa Milà to explore the iconic rooftop terrace early in the morning before crowds build up. Book tickets online in advance (approx. €28–30 per person). Enjoy breakfast at a nearby café first.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — take the skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica (pre-booked). The afternoon slot allows you to see the stunning interior light effects as sunlight streams through the stained-glass windows. The tour lasts approximately 1.5–2 hours. Explore the surrounding Gaudí Park area afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore the neighbourhood's buzzing evening scene. Walk along Carrer d'Enric Granados — a pedestrian boulevard lined with terraces — for pre-dinner drinks, then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Federal Café in Eixample — excellent coffee, avocado toast, and eggs. Approx. €10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Sagrada Família — try one of the casual restaurants on Avinguda de Gaudí or grab a fresh sandwich and juice from a local market. Budget approx. €12–18.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moments or a mid-range Catalan restaurant in Eixample such as La Pepita or Bar Calders. Expect €25–35 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — this is one of Barcelona's most visited sites and afternoon slots sell out quickly, especially in August. Wear comfortable shoes as there is significant walking involved.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — take the metro or walk down to the Gothic Quarter for a self-guided or small-group walking tour through Barcelona's medieval heart. Highlights include the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the Roman ruins visible through the Museu d'Història de Barcelona. Transition into the trendy El Born neighbourhood to admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the Mercat de Santa Caterina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Raval — join a small-group food tour through El Raval's local tapas bars and vermouth spots. This is a fantastic way to taste authentic Catalan cuisine including patatas bravas, jamón, anchovies, and house vermouth. Tours typically run 3–4 hours and include multiple stops. Book in advance (approx. €55–75 per person including food and drinks).
day_by_day.evening: After the food tour, take a relaxed evening walk back through El Born. Browse the boutique shops and galleries, then settle in for cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Born as a preview of tomorrow's nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Bar del Pla in El Born or a traditional granja (milk bar) in the Gothic Quarter — try a traditional pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and café amb llet. Approx. €8–12.
meals.lunch: Covered by the Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Raval — multiple tastings included in the tour price.
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the food tour — you'll likely still be full! Try a simple plate of charcuterie and cheese with a glass of Catalan wine at Bar Brutal in El Born. Approx. €15–20.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter can be very crowded in August — start the morning walk early (by 9:00–9:30) to enjoy the medieval streets before tour groups arrive. Comfortable walking shoes are essential as the streets are cobblestoned.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach Morning — take the metro or a leisurely walk down to Barceloneta Beach for a relaxed morning swim and sunbathing. August weather in Barcelona is typically hot and sunny (28–32°C), making this perfect beach weather. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for comfort (approx. €10–15). Explore the beachfront promenade and the Barceloneta neighbourhood's colourful streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fresh Seafood Paella Lunch at a beachfront restaurant — enjoy a classic seafood paella or fideuà (noodle paella) at one of the established restaurants along Passeig Marítim. After lunch, visit the nearby Barcelona Aquarium or explore the Port Olímpic marina area. Alternatively, take a relaxed stroll back through El Born for afternoon shopping and a gelato.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife Experience in Sant Pere & El Born — begin the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Born (try Bar Paradiso or Mirablau for views). Progress through the neighbourhood's vibrant bar scene, then head to Sant Pere for live music or dancing. Barcelona's nightlife typically starts late — dinner at 21:00, bars from 23:00, clubs from 01:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a beach chiringuito (beach bar) or café near Barceloneta — fresh orange juice, croissant, and coffee. Approx. €8–10.
meals.lunch: Seafood paella lunch at La Mar Salada or Barceloneta restaurant on Passeig Marítim. Budget approx. €30–45 per person — a worthwhile mid-range splurge for fresh, authentic paella.
meals.dinner: Dinner before the nightlife crawl at El Xampanyet in El Born — a beloved traditional bar serving cava and tapas. Approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta Beach gets extremely crowded by midday in August — arrive by 09:30 to secure a good spot. Be vigilant with belongings on the beach as pickpocketing can occur. For the nightlife experience, pace yourself — Barcelona's evening scene runs very late and it's easy to overdo it early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Park Güell — Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park offering panoramic views over Barcelona. Book the Monumental Zone timed entry ticket in advance (approx. €10). Arrive early to beat the heat and the crowds. Explore the iconic mosaic terrace, the Hypostyle Room, and the gingerbread gatehouses. Enjoy the sweeping city views before heading back down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Eixample for a final afternoon of leisure. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies — a world-class contemporary art museum housed in a stunning Modernista building, just steps from your hotel (approx. €12 entry). Alternatively, spend the afternoon browsing the upscale boutiques and design shops along Passeig de Gràcia and Rambla de Catalunya for souvenirs and last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — celebrate your Barcelona trip with a special dinner at a quality Catalan restaurant. Enjoy traditional dishes like escalivada, croquetas, and crema catalana paired with a bottle of Priorat or Penedès wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Forn de Sant Jaume or a neighbourhood bakery in Eixample before heading to Park Güell — pastries, coffee, and fresh fruit. Approx. €8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Gràcia neighbourhood near Park Güell — a charming village-like area with excellent mid-range restaurants and café terraces. Try La Pepita Gràcia or a local menú del día. Approx. €15–20.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Disfrutar (splurge option, book well ahead) or a more accessible but excellent choice like Cervecería Catalana or Bodega 1900 in Eixample. Budget approx. €35–50 per person for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry tickets must be booked online in advance — walk-up tickets are rarely available in August. The hike up to the park is steep; consider taking the Bus 24 or a taxi to the main entrance. If departing Barcelona on Day 6 or later, use this evening to pack and prepare. Keep your T-Casual metro card topped up for airport travel.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from El Prat Airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel in Eixample and freshen up. Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the iconic Modernista facades — including Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside. Stop at a local patisserie for a welcome coffee and pastry to ease into Barcelona time.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Eixample restaurant such as Disfrutar or Lasarte (both Michelin-starred), offering avant-garde Catalan cuisine. After dinner, enjoy a nightcap at a sophisticated cocktail bar in the Eixample — try Dry Martini Barcelona for a classic, refined experience.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Light welcome snack at a local Eixample café upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Grab a premium bocadillo or charcuterie board at a stylish Eixample deli or café near the hotel after settling in.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Disfrutar (avant-garde tasting menu) or Lasarte (Michelin-starred Basque-Catalan cuisine) — reservations strongly recommended well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer for a seamless luxury arrival. Contact the hotel concierge in advance to confirm dinner reservations at your chosen Michelin-starred restaurant. Pack light layers as August evenings in Barcelona can still be warm but breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a gourmet breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby upscale café such as Federal Café or Parking Pizza Brunch in Eixample. Afterward, explore the Eixample's architectural gems on foot — visit the exterior and interior of Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with a priority-access ticket, enjoying the rooftop terrace views over the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagrada Família Skip-the-Line Guided Tour — the afternoon slot is ideal for lighting inside the basilica. A private or small-group guided tour will illuminate Gaudí's genius, the symbolism of the facades, and the breathtaking stained-glass nave. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Afterward, relax at a nearby terrace café in the Gràcia neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Nightlife Experience in Sant Pere & El Born — begin with sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar such as El Nacional's terrace or Bar Calders, then move into El Born's vibrant bar scene. Enjoy craft cocktails at Paradiso (world-renowned speakeasy-style bar) before exploring the neighbourhood's late-night venues.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel or Federal Café — avocado toast, fresh juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Tapas lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — premium patatas bravas, croquetas, and fresh seafood montaditos.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Nacional Barcelona — a stunning multi-concept food hall in a restored 1889 building offering Catalan cuisine, oyster bar, and craft cocktails in one iconic space.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família skip-the-line tickets and La Pedrera priority access well in advance — these sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Request a private guide for Sagrada Família for the most immersive experience. Paradiso bar operates on a first-come basis; arrive before 22:00 to avoid long queues.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — join a small-group or private guided walking tour through Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter. Highlights include the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the ancient Roman ruins beneath the city. Transition into the trendy El Born neighbourhood to admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the Mercat de Santa Caterina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Raval — join a curated small-group food tour through El Raval's authentic local tapas bars and vermouth spots. Sample traditional vermouth with olives, house-made croquetas, pan con tomate, and seasonal pintxos at carefully selected local haunts. A perfect mid-afternoon cultural and culinary immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a refined evening. Visit the rooftop terrace of Casa Milà at dusk for the 'La Pedrera by Night' experience (live jazz and cava on the rooftop — check seasonal schedule). Cap the night with dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda or Moments (Mandarin Oriental) for an elegant Catalan fine-dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Hofmann Pastisseria in El Born for world-class croissants and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Included in the Tapas & Vermouth Crawl — multiple tasting stops across El Raval.
meals.dinner: Moments Restaurant at Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — two Michelin stars, modern Catalan haute cuisine with an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter tour — cobblestone streets can be uneven. The El Raval food tour typically runs 3–4 hours; confirm the meeting point with the tour operator. Book 'La Pedrera by Night' tickets in advance as they are extremely popular in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach Morning — take a short taxi or metro ride from Eixample to Barceloneta. Enjoy a relaxed morning on the beach with a premium sun lounger and parasol rental at one of the upscale beach clubs such as W Barcelona Beach Club or Ola Bar. Swim in the Mediterranean and soak up the summer atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fresh Seafood Paella Lunch at a top beachside restaurant — dine at La Mar Salada or Els Pescadors for an exceptional seafood paella or fideuà (Catalan noodle paella), paired with local white wine or cava. After lunch, take a scenic walk along the Port Olímpic marina. Return to the hotel for a rest and to prepare for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Nightlife Experience in Sant Pere & El Born — begin the evening with pre-dinner cocktails at the rooftop bar of Hotel Arts Barcelona overlooking the sea and city skyline. Move to El Born for dinner at Bar del Pla or Bormuth, then dive into Barcelona's legendary nightlife — visit Razzmatazz or Sala Apolo for world-class DJ sets, or opt for the more intimate Marula Café for jazz-infused club nights.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a Barceloneta café or beach club — fresh fruit, yogurt, and café con leche before hitting the beach.
meals.lunch: Premium seafood paella at La Mar Salada or Els Pescadors — fresh catch of the day, local wine pairing included.
meals.dinner: Tapas dinner at Bar del Pla in El Born — elevated Catalan tapas in a vibrant, authentic setting before the nightlife begins.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season — the beach gets crowded by midday, so arrive by 9:30–10:00 to secure the best spot. Pre-book a premium sun lounger at a beach club for the full luxury experience. Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs typically fill up after midnight, so plan dinner around 21:00–22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Eixample — enjoy a long, indulgent hotel breakfast. Take a last stroll along Passeig de Gràcia for any remaining shopping at luxury boutiques (Loewe, Massimo Dutti flagship, or local artisan shops). Visit the interior of Casa Batlló with a premium after-hours or early-access ticket if not yet explored — the immersive audio-visual experience is unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Park Güell for a final dose of Gaudí magic — book a timed-entry ticket to the Monumental Zone to see the iconic mosaic terrace, Hypostyle Room, and dragon staircase. The hilltop location offers sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona. Afterward, head to Gràcia neighbourhood for a final coffee and browse the charming local market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium restaurant of choice — consider Alkimia (one Michelin star, inventive Catalan cuisine) or Cinc Sentits (Michelin-starred, modern Catalan tasting menu with wine pairing). End the evening with a final cocktail at Dry Martini or the rooftop bar of your hotel, toasting to an unforgettable Barcelona experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet hotel breakfast — take your time with fresh pastries, eggs, charcuterie, and cava if available.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Gràcia neighbourhood — try La Pepita for creative montaditos or a seasonal tasting menu at a local bistro.
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu dinner at Cinc Sentits or Alkimia — multi-course Catalan haute cuisine with premium wine pairing. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed-entry tickets must be booked in advance online — August slots fill up very quickly. If departing early the following morning, arrange a private transfer the night before and confirm luggage storage at the hotel if needed. Consider purchasing a bottle of local cava or artisan olive oil as a luxury souvenir from the Boqueria or a Gràcia deli.

query: Barcelona architecture and nightlife, $2000, 5 days, August 2026 from NYC
